plainEnglish.text: Would authorize the City of East Palo Alto to issue up to $125,000,000 in general obligation bonds, repaid from property taxes, to buy land for a civic center and for recreational facilities and to improve the water and stormwater systems.
plainEnglish.excerpt: Measure O would authorize the City to issue up to $125,000,000 in general obligation bonds to finance the acquisition, construction, and improvement of the following:

yes.text: A yes vote authorizes the City to issue up to $125,000,000 in general obligation bonds for the public improvements stated in the measure.
yes.excerpt: Voting “Yes” would mean authorizing the City to issue up to $125,000,000 in general obligation bonds for use on the public improvements stated in the measure and briefly summarized above.

no.text: A no vote means the City would not be authorized to issue the bonds.
no.excerpt: Voting “No” would mean the City would not be authorized to issue the bonds.

fiscal.text: Estimated average annual tax rate of $105.26 per $100,000 of assessed value (highest about $114.41 per $100,000, projected from fiscal year 2028-2029), collected through fiscal year 2057-2058; estimated total debt service $268,205,658 if all bonds are issued.
fiscal.excerpt: The City estimates that the highest tax rate that would be required to be levied is approximately $114.41 per $100,000 of assessed value, which the City projects would begin to apply in fiscal year 2028-2029. The City also estimates that the average annual tax rate that would be required to be levied is $105.26 per $100,000 of assessed value, with the final fiscal year in which the tax would be collected being 2057-2058. The City also estimates that the total debt service, including the principal and interest, that would be required to be repaid if all the bonds are issued and sold is $268,205,658.

argAgainst.text: The argument against says that asking voters to go into bond debt shows that everything in the current budget is being treated as more important than the projects listed in the measure.
argAgainst.excerpt: They are admitting that everything in the current budget is more important than the projects listed in this ballot measure.
argAgainst.location: Primary argument against, page 4 (text layer of scanned PDF)

plainEnglish.text: Would replace Redwood City Municipal Code Chapter 42 with a new chapter that limits rent increases on multifamily housing built before February 1, 1995, expands just-cause eviction protections to most rental housing, and increases relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
